actions: Reproduced the r111 rare-event abstraction and tested variance-adaptive entry betting; found model-specific negative evidence that predictable-Kelly and fixed mixtures did not beat a single lambda=1 factor in certification speed.
Tested smaller and multiscale harm betting under gradual drift; found no improvement over lambda=1 in the held synthetic abstraction.
Derived continuous proposal control from conditionally unbiased second-moment observations and validated a rolling controller on independent landscapes.
Derived bounded expert losses from the defensive proposal floor epsilon_min=0.6, proved convex-mixture second-moment upper bounding, and identified exact zero-loss event-time compression.
Constructed and held-out tested an event-time Fixed-Share-style proposal mixture over epsilon={0.6,0.8,1.0}.
Separated cheap LLM-judge/state signals as proposal guidance from sparse high-fidelity truth labels for future agent-specific multifidelity rare-event evaluation.
Persisted r112 and r113 certificates/checkpoints and advanced role-local LATEST by CAS/readback discipline.

result_summary.rolling_controller: On held-out gradual drift, rolling second-moment control reduced cumulative variance by 5.05% versus fixed epsilon=0.6 and 4.29% versus binary e-CUSUM fallback; from epsilon=0.8 the reductions were 2.84% and 2.64% respectively.
result_summary.event_fixed_share: A performance-tuned bounded-loss event-time Fixed-Share-style mixture nearly matched rolling control: 4.98% variance reduction versus fixed epsilon=0.6 and 2.85% versus fixed epsilon=0.8, ending 0.78% and 1.06% above a phasewise oracle grid.
result_summary.formal_status: Conditional-unbiasedness, bounded-loss construction, convex-mixture second-moment bound and zero-loss event compression have direct derivations. The aggressive eta/share used in engineering validation is not yet theorem-tuned; no production-agent or AGI conclusion follows.

termination_cause: finite invocation boundary with substantive progress; frontier remains nonempty
exact_next_action: Instantiate the Herbster-Warmuth Fixed Share tracking-regret bound on the event-time bounded loss sequence for J=3 and an explicit switch budget; map it through B=25/9 and S(q_mix)<=sum_j w_j S(q_j) into cumulative proposal variance units. Compare theorem-tuned parameters with the aggressive eta=16/share=0.01 engineering setting under abrupt, gradual and recurring drift on held-out common-random paths. In parallel, prototype judge-guided proposal plus sparse high-fidelity correction on agent traces while preserving defensive base support and explicit likelihood correction.
